indian.headline: Indian markets fell sharply today; banking sector's 3.2% crash dragged Sensex and Nifty lower.
indian.lead: Indian markets fell sharply today; banking sector's 3.2% crash dragged Sensex and Nifty lower.
indian.brief: Sensex dropped 1.77% and Nifty 50 fell 1.75%, with Bank Nifty plunging 3.17%, erasing ₹5.17 trillion in market value and snapping a four-week winning streak.
why: Banking sector collapsed 3.2%, pulling down Bank Nifty by 3.17% despite IT gains of 1.7%, as the heavyweight financial stocks that had driven the recent rally reversed sharply.
Metals fell 3.7% and energy dropped 1.8%, reflecting broad-based selling pressure that overwhelmed pockets of strength in IT and realty.
Nifty 50 posted its worst day since July, breaking a four-week rally during which it was Asia's top performer, signalling profit-taking after a strong run.

drivers: Banking sector's 3.2% decline weighed heavily, as ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and SBI—which had driven 45% of recent Nifty gains—reversed course today.
IT's modest 1.7% gain failed to offset weakness in metals (-3.7%), energy (-1.8%), and auto (-1.0%), leaving the index underwater.
Bank Nifty's 3.17% crash dragged the broader Nifty lower, as banking is a core Nifty component and the sector's sharp selloff overwhelmed IT and realty gains.
Energy and metals combined weakness added downward pressure, with energy down 1.8% and metals down 3.7%, offsetting IT's resilience.
ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and SBI—the 'Big 5' drivers of recent rallies—sold off sharply today as profit-taking hit the heavyweight lenders after weeks of foreign investor inflows.
Banking sector's 3.2% decline signals a broader rotation out of financials after the index touched elevated levels on the back of ₹1 lakh crore in FII inflows.

indian.narrative:
Indian equities ended sharply lower on 24 November as a broad selloff erased ₹5.17 trillion in market value. The Sensex fell 1.77% and Nifty 50 dropped 1.75%, marking the benchmark index's worst day since July and snapping a four-week rally that had made India Asia's top-performing market. Bank Nifty crashed 3.17%, dragged down by ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and SBI—the five mega-cap stocks that had accounted for 45% of recent Nifty gains and benefited from foreign investor buying of ₹1 lakh crore. Weakness in metals (-3.7%) and energy (-1.8%) added to selling pressure, though IT held firm with a 1.7% gain.

The sharp reversal signals profit-taking after a nearly month-long rally that had driven valuations higher. While the broader market remains supported by strong foreign inflows, today's move shows investors are willing to book gains on the heaviest-weighted stocks. Outside the index moves, Shriram Finance's upcoming entry into the Sensex (replacing Trent on 21 December) and Mahanadi Coalfields' imminent listing (27 November) highlight ongoing structural shifts, while SEBI's warning against fake WhatsApp and Telegram trading groups underscores rising retail investor vigilance.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: No explicit global catalyst mentioned; domestic factors drove the fall.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: Recent ₹1 lakh crore inflows may have slowed; banking stocks sold off despite foreign support.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Energy sector down 1.8%, suggesting oil weakness is pressuring the index.

indian.watch: Monitor if the banking sector stabilises tomorrow or if selling extends; watch Mahanadi Coalfields listing (27 Nov) for retail appetite.

us.headline: US stocks surge on Nvidia CEO return; tech leads broad rally across global markets.
us.lead: US stocks surge on Nvidia CEO return; tech leads broad rally across global markets.
us.brief: S&P 500 rose 4.73%, Nasdaq jumped 6.51%, and Dow gained 3.01% as technology stocks climbed 9.0%.
why: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, triggering 31.5% stock surge and restoring $1 trillion in value, reigniting confidence in AI trade.
Asian markets rallied 4.6% on Nvidia news; South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.19% as AI-linked stocks recovered from 10-month lows.
CrowdStrike–Zscaler $44 billion merger announced, signaling consolidation in cybersecurity as AI-driven cyberattacks accelerate.
Lower oil prices eased inflation concerns, pushing Japanese bond yields to two-week lows and broadening market risk appetite.
us.narrative:
US markets posted a strong day as Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO sent shockwaves through global equities. The chipmaker's stock soared 31.5%, recovering roughly $1 trillion in lost value and reigniting the artificial intelligence trade that had cooled after Huang's surprise resignation on November 12. The Nasdaq outpaced the broader market with a 6.51% gain, while the S&P 500 and Dow rose 4.73% and 3.01% respectively. Tech stocks led all sectors with a 9.0% jump, though financials (+2.0%) and healthcare (+1.2%) also climbed. Energy was the lone underperformer, down 1.1%.

The optimism rippled globally: South Korea's KOSPI index surged 7.19% as AI-linked stocks rebounded from their weakest levels in a decade. Meanwhile, news of CrowdStrike acquiring Zscaler for $44 billion underscored strong appetite for cybersecurity consolidation as AI-powered cyberattacks intensify. On the economic front, falling oil prices eased inflation worries, prompting Japanese government bond yields to slide to two-week lows. The backdrop remains risk-on, with investors betting on AI-driven growth offsetting near-term macro headwinds.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Jensen Huang's return as CEO triggered surge and AI trade revival.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Global electrical infrastructure spending projected over next decade, driven by AI and EV demand.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: AI optimism and falling oil prices fuel appetite; cybersecurity M&A activity rising.

us.watch: Monitor Nvidia execution under Huang and fallout from CrowdStrike–Zscaler deal approval.
